name: Congestion and breakouts
summary: Ongoing congestion is often a sign of an imbalanced routine or a compromised skin barrier, rather than a problem with the underlying skin itself.
statement: Ongoing congestion is often a sign of *an imbalanced routine or a compromised skin barrier*, rather than a problem with the underlying skin itself.
happening: Ongoing congestion usually reflects a combination of oil production, skin barrier function and the skin's own renewal cycle, rather than a single product or habit. Because the underlying cause varies between patients, an effective plan usually starts with understanding what kind of congestion is occurring before recommending a treatment.

factors.title: Cumulative exposure
factors.text: Congestion usually reflects cumulative exposure and skin behaviour over years, not a single recent cause.

factors.title: Barrier and turnover
factors.text: Changes to the skin barrier and cell turnover rate influence how visible congestion becomes over time.

factors.title: Individual variation
factors.text: How congestion presents and responds to treatment varies meaningfully between skin types.

recommendedText: Considered as a deep-cleansing option for ongoing congestion, particularly where hydration is also a concern.
alongsideText: Often assessed alongside, since these concerns frequently share the same treatment options.

steps.title: Assessment first
steps.text: We look at the skin and the routine around it, since ongoing congestion often reflects an imbalanced routine or barrier.

steps.title: Routine first
steps.text: The daily routine is adjusted before, or alongside, any in-clinic treatment.

steps.title: Gentle clearing
steps.text: In-clinic treatments clear congestion gently, so the barrier is supported rather than stripped.

steps.title: Ongoing review
steps.text: The plan is reviewed at follow-up and adjusted as the skin settles.
